p: doings of the land of Egypt: You shall preserve yourselves from these abominations following, which the Egyptians and Canaanites use.
I am the LORD: And therefore you ought to serve me alone, as my people.
uncover their nakedness: That is, to lie with her, though it be under title of marriage.
wife shalt thou not uncover: Which is your stepmother.
sister: Either by father or mother, born in marriage or otherwise.
nakedness: They are her children whose shame you have uncovered.
father's brother: Which your uncle discovers.
brother's wife: Because the idolaters, among whom God's people had dwelt and would dwell, were given to these horrible incests, God charges his own to beware of them.
vex her: By seeing your affection more bent to her sister than to her.
apart for her uncleanness: Or while she has her period.

Molech: Which was an idol of the Ammonites, to whom they burned and sacrificed their children, 2Ki 23:10. This seemed to be the chief and principal of all idols: and as the Jews write, was of a great stature, and hollow within, having seven places or chambers within him: one was to receive meal that was offered: another turtle doves: the third, a sheep: the fourth, a ram: the fifth a calf: the sixth an ox: the seventh a child. This idols face was like a calf: his hands were ever stretched out to receive gifts: his priests were called Chemarims, 2Ki 23:5, Ho 10:5, Zep 1:4.
visit the iniquity thereof upon it: I will punish the land where such incestuous marriages and pollutions are tolerated.
vomiteth out her inhabitants: He compares the wicked to evil humours and overeating, which corrupt the stomach, and oppress nature, and therefore must be cast out by vomit.
spued out the nations that were: Both for their wicked marriages, unnatural copulations, idolatry or spiritual whoredom with Molech and such like abominations.
be cut off from among their: Either by the civil sword or by some plague that God will send upon such.
